Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust share repurchase activity, strategic capital deployment plans including acquisitions and new products, the effectiveness of our reinsurance program, improving loss ratio trends amid favorable claims frequency and severity dynamics, ongoing expense ratio improvements through commission and operating cost efficiencies, and solid investment income yields. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our Parametric Climate Solutions product and its rapid adoption among commercial clients facing heightened climate risks.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. As John mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $3.25 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included accelerated share repurchases, prudent capital allocation toward growth opportunities, strong reinsurance recoveries, favorable loss and expense trends, and elevated investment returns. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $650 million, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income and alternatives segments. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with 620% Total Adjusted Capital ratio.

Before diving deeper into our segment results, let me provide some color on our capital deployment, starting with share repurchase activity, which remains a cornerstone of our disciplined shareholder returns framework. In Q3, we executed $750 million in share repurchases under our ongoing program, bringing year-to-date activity to $2.8 billion. This represents a 35% acceleration from the $2.1 billion we deployed in the first nine months of 2023, reflecting our robust free cash flow generation and confidence in the intrinsic value of our franchise. At an average price of $148 per share—about 12x our forward combined ratio and 1.4x book value—we retired approximately 5.1 million shares in the quarter, or 1.2% of our outstanding float. Post-quarter end, we've opportunistically added another $150 million, leaving us with $4.2 billion remaining under our current $10 billion authorization, which we expanded by $3 billion at our June board meeting.

This pace is underpinned by several technical and strategic tailwinds unique to our industry. First, our property-casualty book continues to deliver industry-leading underwriting margins, with a Q3 combined ratio of 92.4%, down 180 basis points year-over-year, driven by rate adequacy gains of 9.2% across our commercial lines portfolio—think excess & surplus and middle-market workers' comp, where we've seen hardening persist amid social inflation pressures. This has unlocked $1.2 billion in deployable capital for the quarter alone, after accounting for our target RBC ratio of 550% and reinsurance renewals at the January 1 Florida Hurricane Catastrophe layer.

Investment-wise, our fixed-income portfolio yielded 4.8% annualized in Q3, bolstered by the Fed's terminal rate environment, allowing us to recycle maturities from our $45 billion portfolio into higher-coupon corporates and RMBS without compromising our AA- rating. We've also layered in $500 million from our catastrophe bond issuance earlier this year—the 'Unity Re Cat 2024-1' deal—which priced at a tight 4.25% all-in spread, providing multi-year protection against U.S. severe convective storm and California wildfire perils.

Regionally, our U.S. operations fueled 70% of this activity, with strong performance in our Southeast and Gulf Coast books offsetting $220 million in Hurricane Idalia claims. In contrast, EMEA deployment was more measured at $180 million, as we navigated Solvency II capital add-ons from the Turkish earthquakes' ripple effects on our reinsurance recoverables. APAC remains opportunistic, with $120 million repurchased amid softer life reinsurance pricing, but we're monitoring China's property market for potential portfolio optimization.

From a technical standpoint, we've refined our at-the-market repurchase facility with our counterparties—JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs—to incorporate VWAP-based algorithmic execution, which has minimized market impact to under 15 basis points of daily volume. This 10b5-1 plan allows us to repurchase efficiently during earnings blackouts, aligning with peers like Chubb and Travelers, who've similarly ramped programs post-rate cycle inflection.

Strategically, these buybacks are not just tactical; they're a signal of our undervaluation versus comps trading at 14x P/E. By reducing shares outstanding by 4.5% YTD, we're enhancing EPS accretion—projected at 8-10% for FY 2025—and supporting our progressive dividend policy, which we raised 12% to $1.40 per share last quarter. This complements our M&A war chest, as we eye bolt-on opportunities in cyber and parametric insurance, much like Markel's recent plays in insurtech. Looking forward, we expect to deploy another $3-4 billion through year-end 2025, contingent on sustained attritional loss ratios below 60% and no major cat corridor disruptions.

Building on that capital discipline, I'd like to outline our broader capital deployment strategy for the balance of 2024 and into 2025. We've maintained a fortress balance sheet throughout this volatile environment, ending Q3 with $18.7 billion in deployable capital—up 12% year-over-year—supported by our industry-leading 620% TAC ratio and a pristine 95.2% combined ratio ex-cat on a 12-month rolling basis. This positions us exceptionally well to execute on both opportunistic inorganic growth and organic innovation, all while delivering superior shareholder returns.

Our capital allocation framework remains disciplined and multi-pronged, prioritizing returns above an 11% ROE hurdle rate, with a clear bias toward high-conviction opportunities in P&C, specialty lines, and emerging risks like cyber and climate. For the next 24 months, we're targeting the deployment of approximately $3.2 billion, allocated as follows: 40% or $1.3 billion toward tuck-in acquisitions and strategic partnerships; 30% or $950 million into product innovation and technology platforms; 20% or $640 million in share repurchases; and the balance toward progressive dividend growth and opportunistic bolt-ons.

On acquisitions and M&A, we've been active but selective, focusing on assets that accretively enhance our book of business, geographic footprint, and specialty capabilities without compromising underwriting discipline. In Q1, we closed our $425 million acquisition of Midwest Heritage Mutual, a super-regional P&C carrier with $1.2 billion in GWP focused on commercial auto and workers' comp in the US heartland. This deal is already delivering synergies—we've realized $35 million in annual expense savings through our shared services platform and improved the block's loss ratio by 220 basis points via our proprietary telematics and GLMs. Post-close, it's contributing 25 bps to our statutory ROE.

Looking ahead, we've earmarked $800 million for two to three additional tuck-ins. We're in late-stage discussions for a cyber reinsurance platform from a European peer, similar to the AXIS Capital model, which would add $300 million in annualized GWP at a sub-90% combined ratio. This aligns with the 25% CAGR in global cyber premiums through 2028, per McKinsey estimates, amid escalating ransomware attacks—up 150% YoY per Chainalysis data. Regionally, we're prioritizing Asia-Pacific, where insurtech penetration remains below 5% versus 15% in the US. Expect a $200-300 million deal for a Singapore-based embedded insurance provider, bolstering our motor and health partnerships with ride-hailing giants like Grab, targeting 20% premium growth in that corridor.

In Europe, regulatory tailwinds from Solvency II reforms are creating carve-outs; we're eyeing UK liability portfolios strained by the Ogden rate reset, much like Aviva's playbook. No mega-deals on the horizon—our track record shows tuck-ins yield 2-3x higher IRR than transformercials, with integration ROIs hitting 15% within 18 months.

On new products and organic innovation, we're investing $950 million to launch and scale next-gen offerings, leveraging our $500 million tech stack modernization completed last year. This includes a 25% ramp in AI/ML underwriting capabilities, which have already shaved 80 bps off our expense ratio in personal lines pilots.

Key launches include Parametric Climate Solutions, rolling out nationwide in Q4, with $150 million initial capacity. Inspired by Swiss Re's successes, these trigger-based products cover hurricane wind speeds and wildfire smoke plumes—critical as US cat losses hit $165 billion in 2023 per Swiss Re sigma. Early adoption in Florida and California shows 30% attachment rates among commercial real estate clients, with blended loss ratios under 60%.

Embedded Cyber for SMEs, partnering with fintechs like Stripe and Shopify, we're embedding $50k-$5M cyber policies into e-commerce platforms. This targets the $10 trillion underserved SME market, where cyber claims frequency rose 40% YoY per Coalition data. Our Actuarial AI engine prices risks in real-time using external data feeds from CrowdStrike, aiming for $400 million GWP by YE25 at 92% combined.

Usage-Based Health in APAC, expanding our VitalTrack telematics from auto into life & health, with wearable integrations via Apple Health. Pilots in Indonesia and India project 15% lower morbidity assumptions, unlocking $250 million in embedded value.

These initiatives are backed by a $300 million capex commitment to cloud-native platforms on AWS and Snowflake, driving a targeted 50 bps annual improvement in our operating expense ratio toward our 28% long-term goal.

Regionally, US P&C remains our growth engine at 65% of GWP, with California wildfire exposure managed via 10% rate adequacy hikes and 20% reinsurance tower expansions. Europe contributes 20%, where we're de-risking legacy annuities via longevity swaps. APAC is the star, growing 22% YoY to 15% of the book, fueled by India's IRDAI-mandated motor reforms.

Strategically, this deployment mix reflects our view of a bifurcating market: hardening rates in catastrophe-exposed lines funding expansion into resilient specialties, where we're underwriting at 85-90% combined ratios. With investment yields at 4.8% on our $45 billion portfolio—boosted by the Fed's hikes—we're generating $2.1 billion in recurring income, providing dry powder amid peers trading at 1.2x book.

On shareholder returns, our $640 million buyback authorization has $400 million remaining; we've repurchased 4.2 million shares at an average 12% discount to tangible book. We'll raise the quarterly dividend 8% to $0.42/share next month, marking our 19th consecutive increase, for a 2.8% yield.

Turning to investment income yield, which came in at 4.15% on an annualized basis—up 85 basis points year-over-year and 22 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our strongest quarterly yield since Q4 2021, driven by a favorable reinvestment environment amid the Fed's rate hiking cycle, and it exceeded our internal guidance of 3.9% to 4.1%. For context, this yield is calculated as net investment income divided by the average amortized cost of our invested assets, excluding funds withheld under reinsurance treaties, which aligns with our NAIC statutory reporting.

Reinvestment yields were the standout performer at 5.25%, a 240 basis point improvement from 3.01% a year ago. We've been aggressively redeploying maturities and cash flows into higher-yielding securities, capitalizing on the inverted yield curve. Our fixed income portfolio, which constitutes 72% of our $145 billion general account—now stands at an embedded book yield of 4.45%, with new money yields pushing toward 5.5% in the intermediate and long-duration buckets. Corporate bonds, at 45% of the portfolio, delivered a segment yield of 4.85%, benefiting from spread tightening in investment-grade names from tech-adjacent issuers while maintaining a conservative average credit quality of AA-.

Equities, comprising 12% of assets, contributed 8.2% to the yield through a mix of dividend aristocrats and covered call overlays, generating $285 million in income, up 14% YoY. Our alternatives bucket—15% of the portfolio, including core real estate, infrastructure funds, and a modest 3% allocation to energy MLPs—yielded 6.1%, providing inflation-hedging ballast amid sticky CPI around 3.2%.

On trends, this yield reflects a multi-quarter inflection. Post-2022's rate shock, we've seen portfolio duration extend modestly to 5.7 years from 4.9, optimizing convexity without excessive rate risk—our effective duration matches our P&C liability tail of 5.2 years under our ALM framework. Year-to-date, we've captured 110 basis points of spread compression in municipals, which make up 18% of fixed income and yielded 3.95% tax-adjusted.

Regionally, our U.S. investments—60% of the portfolio—drove 4.35% yields, fueled by 10-year Treasuries at 4.2% and robust CMBS spreads. Europe, at 20%, lagged at 3.2% due to ECB policy divergence, though we've shifted into UK gilts yielding 4.1%. Asia-Pacific, 15%, hit 4.8% via JGBs and AUD corporates. Emerging markets remain underweight at 5%, focused on high-grade LatAm sovereigns.

Strategically, our proprietary ALM platform, enhanced with BlackRock's Aladdin, has enabled dynamic laddering—deploying 40% of maturities into 5-10 year buckets. We've advanced ESG integration, with 28% of new fixed income in sustainable bonds yielding 20bps premium. Dividend reinvestment from equities totaled $420 million.

Looking forward, we guide to a full-year 2024 yield of 4.4% to 4.6%, assuming no recessionary Fed cuts before mid-year. This positions us to deliver peer-leading ROE expansion.

Now, a bit more on expense ratio trends and drivers. In Q3, we delivered a combined ratio of 92.4%, which includes our expense ratio of 92.5%—a 270 basis point improvement year-over-year from 95.2% in Q3 2023, and a 50 basis point sequential improvement from Q2. This marks our sixth consecutive quarter of expense ratio compression, bringing our nine-month trailing expense ratio to 92.8%, down from 94.5% last year. This positions us 110 basis points below the industry average per AM Best.

Commissions and acquisition-related fees represented 24.8% of earned premiums in Q3, flat sequentially but down 80 basis points YoY. This reflects disciplined broker management. In personal lines, independent agent commissions averaged 12.5%, benefiting from digital shifts; we've moved 15% of our book direct-to-consumer, reducing blended costs by 1.2 points. In commercial lines, commissions ticked to 18.2% for specialty programs. Regionally, U.S. steady at 24.5%, Europe down to 23.1% via bancassurance.

Operating expenses came in at 67.7%—improving 190 basis points YoY—driven by 12% reduction in cost per policy. Our Guidewire Cloud migration, 75% complete, slashed policy admin costs by 22%, generating $45 million in savings. AI claims adjudication processed 40% of small auto claims straight-through, cutting LAE to 8.2%. Telematics covers 2.5 million policies.

Regionally, U.S. at 66.5%, Asia-Pacific targeting sub-70%, Europe at 70.4%. Looking ahead, sub-90% by 2026 via gen AI and embedded APIs.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-driven risk selection and advanced modeling.

Today, I'd like to dive into our loss ratio trends and the key drivers behind them—a core metric underscoring our underwriting discipline. We're reporting on both calendar year loss ratio and accident year loss ratio, with prior year development called out separately.

Overall, we delivered a strong Q3 CALR of 63.2%, a 360 basis point improvement from 66.8% last year. Excluding cats at 4.2 points, ex-CAT CALR of 59.1%, our best in a decade.

Claims frequency declined 6.2% YoY. In personal auto—42% of premiums—frequency dropped 8.1% via ApexDrive telematics at 35% penetration, non-renewing high-risks. Homeowners fell 4.5% with smart sensors on 150,000 policies. Commercial dipped 3.8%. U.S. improved 7.1%, APAC 9.4%.

Severity up 7.9% YoY. Auto +10.2% to $12,800 per claim on parts/labor inflation; countered by Direct Repair Program. Homeowners +9.1% to $28,400. Cats $450M total.

Favorable PYD added 1.8 points. Segments: Personal Auto 61.2% ex-CAT, Homeowners 67.8%, Commercial 65.4%, Specialty 58.9%.

Strategic pillars: Dynamic Pricing 2.0 with GLMs, Claims Transformation with Palantir AI saving $85M, Portfolio Optimization exiting underperformers.

For 2024, guide ex-CAT 59-61%.

Another key pillar is the effectiveness of our reinsurance program, optimizing capital efficiency in our $45 billion GWP portfolio across 25 countries.

We ceded $1.45 billion YTD, up 12%, with 32% ceding commissions generating $465 million, bolstering expense ratio by 180 bps. Recoveries $1.12 billion on $1.32 billion losses—85% net recovery rate, holding net loss ratio to 61.2%, net combined 92.4%. Ex-cats, 58.9%.

Treaty structure: Property cat tower $6.2B xs $600M, first layer $1.5B at 2.8% burn cost. Casualty clash $3.8B xs $400M aggregate, multi-year second layer. Retained 15% net on key lines.

Technical initiatives: RMS v5.0 and AIR Touchstone integration, 18% PML reduction via Florida de-risking, parametric pilots triggering $75M.

Regionally: U.S. 92% recoveries, Europe seamless on windstorms, APAC tightened retentions, LATAM mitigated volatility.

Into July renewals, cat pricing softened 5-10%, added $500M sidecars. Leverage 1.8x vs industry 2.3x, unlocking $450M capital relief. This delivers $520M earnings accretion YTD.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, aligning with the strong yields Michael outlined, including 5.25% reinvestment rates and balanced regional allocations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more color on growth in new products like parametric solutions?

John Reynolds: Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, our Parametric Climate Solutions are gaining strong traction with 30% attachment rates in key markets, supporting low loss ratios under 60% and aligning with our $950 million innovation budget.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of inflation on your business?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Inflation has pressured severity up 7.9%, particularly in auto and rebuild costs, but our tech initiatives like telematics and AI claims processing have offset this, maintaining ex-cat loss ratios at 59.1% while driving expense efficiencies.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee: What is the expected impact of Solvency II reforms on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, David. Solvency II tailwinds are creating opportunities, like UK liability carve-outs, allowing us to expand selectively while our reinsurance program— with €1.2B windstorm cover—absorbs pressures seamlessly.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: Thanks. Can you elaborate on reinsurance effectiveness post-recent cats?

Lisa Patel: Sure, Rachel. Our program delivered 85% net recovery on losses, with 92% in U.S. cats like Idalia analogs, far outpacing peers, thanks to our $6.2B cat tower and parametric innovations.

Operator: Our next question is from Tom Rivera with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: Good morning. Thoughts on share repurchases going forward?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Tom. We're on pace for $3-4B more through 2025, with $4.2B authorized remaining, executed efficiently via ATM facilities, signaling confidence in our 92.4% combined ratio and undervaluation.

Operator: Our next question from Sarah Patel with Citigroup.

Sarah Patel: On capital deployment, any updates on M&A pipeline?

Michael Chen: Yes, late-stage talks for cyber platform adding $300M GWP and APAC embedded deal for 20% growth, all accretive above 11% ROE, building on Midwest Heritage synergies.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time.

John Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
